evidence.paraphrase: The teacher feels exhausted and weary of her daily routine.
evidence.quote: She had never felt so tired of it all, it seemed to her.

evidence.paraphrase: She judges the collegiate life as an empty pretense of living.
evidence.quote:
What an idiot she was to give up four years of her life to this round of
work and play and pretence of living!

evidence.paraphrase: She contrasts her present life with an imagined return to her past domestic possibility.
evidence.quote:
Was it too late? Suppose she should go, after all? Suppose she should
go, and all should be as it had been, only a little older, a little more
quiet and peaceful?

evidence.paraphrase: She realizes her absorption in memories caused her to lapse in the classroom.
evidence.quote:
though she had been thinking steadily in German, she had been
talking in English

evidence.paraphrase: Her room is described as artificial and interchangeable with those of other single educated women.
evidence.quote:
It looked utterly impersonal to-day; its very atmosphere was
artificial, typical, a pretended self-sufficiency.

evidence.paraphrase: She attempts to talk herself out of her deep depression about her life.
evidence.quote:
In her own room she tried
to reason herself out of this intolerable depression

evidence.paraphrase: She takes action by mailing a letter, presumably to the man from her past.
evidence.quote:
just before the ten-o'clock bell she slipped out to mail a fat
brown-stamped envelope

evidence.paraphrase: She experiences a heightened joyful state after acting on her hope.
evidence.quote: For the first week she moved in a kind of exaltation.

evidence.paraphrase: A stranger's admiring glance renews her sense of her own attractiveness and worth.
evidence.quote:
But through all her agony of doubt in the days that followed, one shame
was miraculously removed, one hope sang faintly beneath: she, too, had
her power!

evidence.paraphrase: The awaited man arrives, but reaches toward the wrong woman.
evidence.quote:
As she passed by
the little reception-room a tall, eager man made toward her with
outstretched hands.
